source_of_truth: Derived by hand from the build I wrote. /reports has four async:false chunks in its initial set: page-reports.js (small), base1.js (small), reports-grid.js and reports-filters.js (130000 raw each, ~95.6 KB gzip each under gzipSync). The route's TOTAL initial JS is ~200 KB gzip, over 150 KB, but route-heavy-initial-chunk keys off the single LARGEST initial chunk, which is only ~95.6 KB gzip, under the 150 KB cutoff. By the heuristic's own stated scope (largest single chunk, not route total) the honest call and the tool's call agree: no defect. Firing on the total would be a false positive outside the metric's scope. Truth derived from the source only; the tool was not consulted.
provenance: blind generalization: truth derived from source without consulting tool output

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the largest single initial chunk is ~95.6 KB gzip, below the 150 KB cutoff; the heuristic measures the largest single chunk, not the ~200 KB route total, so firing here would be a false positive outside its scope.
